_note: Sports upper secondary schools (urheilulukio) and the application to them (GDD 4.9.3; research session D1, 2026-10-17; used by session S3). Every fact has a `src` index into `sources` (url + the date it was read + how: `page` = the page was opened and read, `search-summary` = only seen in a search result summary and not opened, so check it before relying on it). Cut-offs are the LOWEST accepted points (out of 20) published by the school or the city; `year` is the application year. A missing cut-off is `null` = not found. `athletics`: priority = athletics is named a priority / main sport of the school; offered = athletes of athletics are named there; unverified = nothing found either way (do not assume). `status`: special_task = on the Olympic Committee's list of the 15 sports lukiot with a national special educational task (2026 application); line = a municipal sports line that uses the national criteria. Nothing here is a promise that a place exists in a future year: later years are by rule in S3, with `estimated`.

application.system: The joint application (yhteishaku) in Opintopolku; athletes also answer the 'athlete supplementary questions' (home school, main sport, club and federation, best results of the last three seasons, training group, coach's contact, grade average).

federation_points_to_schools.note: Sammon keskuslukio and Kuopion klassillinen lukio say the federations send their points on 27.4.2026; tests and interviews follow in May.

parts.name: Grade average of the basic education certificate (incl. compulsory PE)
parts.note: Mäkelänrinne scores the average on the scale 4-10; the average of lukio-subjects and PE is weighted.

parts.name: Federation points (sports merit and talent, given by the national sports federation)
School points (the school's own: tests, interview, the training and coaching conditions)

application.federation_scale_note: NOT VERIFIED: the Finnish Athletics Federation's own scale for the 0-5 federation points was not found in public sources (the figure skating federation publishes one). S3 needs a rule: first guess from the TF-juniorit standards (data/standards.json).
application.olympic_committee_guide: The Olympic Committee's guide says the usual minimum is a grade average of 7-7.5 (GDD 4.9.8, read 2026-10-11); the schools above publish their own minima.

centres.note: SUL's athletics centres 2026 as the SUL page lists them: five training managers, in Lahti, Jyväskylä, the capital region, Tampere and Turku. Kuortane, Pajulahti and Vierumäki are partners (camps, coach education), not centres on that page. GDD 4.9 said the five centres include Kuortane: corrected in the GDD notes of D1.

list.name: Capital region athletics centre
list.fee: free membership (16+, upper-secondary student / employed / professional)
list.applications: continuous, to the end of September
list.services: academy card for capital-region facilities, a free Unisport gym card

list.name: Tampere athletics centre
list.fee: 40 EUR (Tampere club / home municipality) or 60 EUR (others), season 2024-25, may be out of date
list.applications: 1-30 Aug and 1-31 Jan; upper-secondary students 1-31 Aug and 1-20 Jan

list.name: Turku athletics centre
list.note: The SUL academy-services page does not describe Turku.

list.name: Jyväskylä athletics centre
list.applications: continuous, to the end of September
list.services: indoor training slots (up to twice a day), expert services at academy rates (sports medicine, physiotherapy, sports psychology, nutrition, testing), study and career guidance
list.note: The post of the centre's training manager was advertised in July 2026 (application closed 2026-07-19), so no coach is linked.

list.name: Lahti-Pajulahti athletics centre
list.services: Pajulahti has an athletics hall and testing services; Lahti stadium has an indoor running track

centres.team_finland_note: SUL pays the academy fee of an athlete in a Team Finland training group when an academy asks for one (SUL academy-services page). Every athlete taken into a second-level sports school joins the TF-nuoret centre activity with their coach (GDD 4.9.8, read 2026-10-11).

schools.name: Mäkelänrinteen lukio
schools.programme: Urheilulukio with the Urhea hall; the athletics line HAA (Helsinki Athletics Academy) accepted sprinters and hurdlers, jumpers and multi-event athletes in 2023; 55 athletics athletes of all event groups (2023). The page on admission does not list middle distance.
schools.morning_practice: The sports athletes train at school in the mornings (school page); days not stated.
schools.dorm: Student apartments on the campus were planned in 2021 ('training, living, meals and study in one place'); not confirmed for 2026.
schools.tests: Spring 2026 suitability tests 27-28 Apr and 6-7 May; registration closed 2026-03-17; good results in the trainability test raise the school points

schools.name: Leppävaaran lukio (urheilulinja)
schools.programme: Sports line (urheilulinja) with over 200 athletes in 37 sports in 2025-26, athletics among them; it uses the national criteria of the sports-school application.
schools.morning_practice: Sports coaching hours (UVA), 90-100 morning practices a year, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday about 8:00-9:30.

schools.name: Pohjois-Haagan yhteiskoulun lukio
schools.programme: Official sports lukio since 2007 with athletes of over 30 sports; athletics is among the largest sport groups; part of the Urhea academy.

schools.name: Brändö gymnasium
schools.programme: On the Olympic Committee's list of the 15 sports lukiot; nothing further was found.

schools.name: Sammon keskuslukio
schools.programme: Athletics is one of the 12 priority sports in 2026-27; the priority sports' training groups are shared with Tredu and the Tampere academy; coaches include the Tampere centre's training manager.
schools.morning_practice: Three morning practices a week: Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday; transport from the Pirkkahalli to school after practice (SUL article 2021, repeated on the school page).

cutoff_history_unlabelled.note: the school page lists 'the lowest averages of the last years' without the years

schools.name: Lahden lyseon lukio
schools.programme: Sports line since 1990 (an official sports lukio since 1994); the four priority sports are football, ice hockey, basketball and athletics; partners: the Päijät-Häme sports academy and the Olympic Committee; students take at least 12 coaching courses (24 credits).

cutoffs.note: the school says the entrance limit 'has been about 15 points in recent years'

schools.tests: 2026: athletics priority-sport test and interview 11 May; coaches interviewed 12-13 and 18 May; the school report is due by 30 Apr

schools.name: Schildtin lukio
schools.programme: Sports line of Gradia; athletics coaches for sprints and hurdles, jumps and multi-events, and throws were named in 2021 (SUL article); priority sports have a school-organised coach in the mornings; the school, training venues and the academy are close together.
schools.morning_practice: Morning sessions with the school's event coach; days and times not stated.

schools.name: Kerttulin lukio (urheilulukio)
schools.programme: Sports lukio; morning practice is general conditioning that is independent of the sport; roughly twice as many applicants as places.
schools.morning_practice: General, sport-independent morning conditioning; athletes can in some cases join their club's morning practice.

schools.name: Kuopion klassillinen lukio
schools.programme: Athletics is one of the school's priority sports (up to 2 school points); interview for applicants with at least 1.8 federation points (interview max 2, discretion 1); linked to the Kuopio area sports academy.

schools.name: Kastellin lukio (urheilulukio)
schools.programme: The key coaching sports are football, ice hockey, volleyball and floorball; athletes of other sports train in an 'other sports' group or with cooperating coaches; the selection test has an interview and physical-motor tests (max 5 points); 124 applicants for 40 places (autumn 2025 application).

schools.name: Ounasvaaran lukio (urheilulukio)
schools.programme: The only official sports lukio in Lapland; athletics is one of its main sports; an applicant can apply for one sport only.

schools.name: Porin lukio (urheilulinja)
schools.programme: Athletics is among the priority sports; sport-specific coaching three times a week; the selection criteria differ from other lukio.

schools.name: Joensuun yhteiskoulun lukio
schools.programme: On the Olympic Committee's list of the 15 sports lukiot; nothing further was found.

schools.name: Sotkamon lukio
schools.programme: National special task for sports; part of the Vuokatti-Ruka sports academy; the training places of the snow sports and pesäpallo are near the dorm.
schools.dorm: A dorm exists near the sports facilities (search summary; details not read).
schools.tests: Entrance tests: federation points at least 2.0, school points at least 2.5, average of subjects and PE at least 7.3; general and sports-line students are chosen in June

schools.name: Vörå samgymnasium (Vöyrin yhteislukio)
schools.programme: On the Olympic Committee's list of the 15 sports lukiot; nothing further was found.

schools.name: Kuortaneen urheilulukio
schools.programme: A special lukio for ice hockey, volleyball, bowling, wrestling, pesäpallo and athletics, next to the Kuortane sports institute (200 m circuit track, jumping and throwing areas, strength rooms, a swimming hall, skiing and running terrain). Athletes train by event group once or twice a day; the 2026-27 page names coaches for high jump and multi-events, javelin, sprints and hammer and has an 'athletics and endurance' group. No middle-distance coach is named on that page.
schools.morning_practice: Event groups train 1-2 times a day; the page does not say which part is in the morning.
schools.dorm: Housing in the institute's school houses: 160-290 EUR a month (a 2016 document, old); the school's own housing page was not read.

vocational.note: Sports vocational schools (urheiluammattiopistot) of the 2026 application: the application gives NO extra points for athletic merit (athlete status comes from the federation's points); applications for the programmes are also accepted all year, deadlines vary by school. Athletics is not checked for any of them.
